---

## 1. Bottom Line

COIN is in a **confirmed, aggressive downtrend** that has just produced its **lowest close in the entire 396-session dataset available (2025-05-01 → 2026-11-25)**. Every swing high and swing low since the 2026-10-30 gap-down break has been lower, and the 50/200 SMA complex is in a bearish alignment with both averages declining. However, the very last bar (2026-11-25) is the **first meaningful bullish anomaly in three weeks**: a 1.05-ATR reversal bar that undercut the prior lows at $101.71–$101.91, wicked down to $94.88, and closed back above the breakdown at $103.72 on 9.82M shares.

**Tactical bias: bearish structure intact, but the short-term risk/reward on fresh shorts is deteriorating.** The confluence of an RSI bullish divergence versus the 2026-11-20 low, a MACD histogram that has contracted from −2.62 to −1.46 over three sessions, and a close back above the failed-breakdown level argue for *caution on new shorts*, not for abandoning the downtrend.

## 4. Trend Structure — Three Distinct Downtrends

**4.1 The secular trend (200 SMA).** The 200 SMA has declined in every session of the available window: $221.84 (2026-07-20) → $171.55 (2026-11-25), a **−22.7%** slide in the average itself. It is falling ~0.32 pts/day.

**4.2 The intermediate trend (50 SMA) and the bearish alignment.** The 50 SMA peaked at **$180.31 on 2026-10-29** and has rolled over hard, now $159.53 — **−11.5% in seven sessions**. Critically, the 50 SMA has been **below the 200 SMA continuously across the entire 130-session indicator window** (2026-07-18: 50 SMA 170.18 vs 200 SMA 219.96 through today: 159.53 vs 171.55). I am not asserting a crossover *date* — the tool window opens with the cross already in effect — but the configuration is unambiguous and both averages are declining into it, so there is no imminent "catching up" repair.

**4.3 Price vs. the moving-average stack — an extreme extension.**

| Reference | Level | Price gap | ATR-normalized distance |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 EMA | 113.04 | −8.24% | 1.04 ATR away |
| 50 SMA | 159.53 | −34.98% | 6.24 ATR away |
| 200 SMA | 171.55 | −39.54% | 7.58 ATR away |
| VWMA (20) | 117.76 | −11.92% | 1.57 ATR away |

Price below *all four* averages, with each average declining, is the definition of an intact bearish stack. Note the **ordering anomaly** worth flagging to traders: the 50 SMA (159.53) is *below* the 200 SMA (171.55), but the 10 EMA (113.04) is far below both — meaning the 50 SMA will only fall toward price at ~1.7 pts/day, so the 50 SMA is roughly **28 ATR-days of travel** away. There is no realistic mean-reversion path to the 50 SMA; it belongs on the overhead-supply map, not the target ladder.

**4.4 The swing structure — texturally clean.**

**4.5 The structural break.** On **2026-10-30** COIN opened at $148.23 and closed at $143.54 (−10.62%) on **20,894,000 shares** — roughly triple the prevailing volume — breaking the September–October consolidation floor (the 10/26–10/29 base of $155.31–$163.60). Everything since has been the post-breakdown drift.

**4.6 Drawdown context.** From the 2026 cycle-high close of $201.05 (2026-09-21) to $103.72 is **−48.4%**. From the dataset's maximum close of $419.78 (2025-07-18) it is **−75.3%**. From the 2026-10-15 close of $183.81 to today is **−43.6% in 29 sessions**.

**4.7 A structural note with real implications.** At $103.72, COIN is trading **below every 2026 low in the dataset** — below the 2026-02-12 low of $139.36 and the 2026-06-25 low of $141.48. There is **no historical support reference beneath the current price in the data I retrieved** (which begins 2025-05-01 at ~$200). This matters enormously for stop placement: a breakdown of $94.88 puts the instrument into genuine price discovery, where volatility tends to *expand* rather than mean-revert.

## 5. Momentum — Oversold, Diverging, but Not Reversed

**5.1 RSI = 28.68.** RSI has been pinned in oversold territory almost continuously since the 2026-10-30 break: 31.91 (10/30) → 29.70 (11/02) → 29.23 (11/16) → 27.44 (11/17) → 25.84 (11/18) → 25.26 (11/19) → **22.94 (11/20, the extreme)** → 29.80 (11/23) → 27.32 (11/24) → 28.68 (11/25). Three weeks of sub-30 readings in a rising-average downtrend is a *condition*, not a *signal* — RSI has been oversold continuously, so "oversold" carries essentially no standalone timing value here.

**5.2 The bullish divergence is real and dated.** Comparing the two most recent lows:
- **2026-11-20: price low $101.71, RSI 22.94**
- **2026-11-25: price low $94.88, RSI 28.68**

Price made a **−6.7% lower low** while RSI made a **+5.7 point higher low** (a 25% increase in the reading). That is a textbook bullish divergence on the RSI oscillator, and it is the single strongest argument for the counter-trend case. I must pair it with the caveat: RSI divergence in a −43% trend reliably produces a **relief rally**, not a durable reversal, and the 2026-11-23 bounce (close $108.78, +6.68%) was fully retraced the next session (2026-11-24 close $102.35) — the first direct evidence that this market fades bounces aggressively.

**5.3 MACD complex.** MACD line −16.09, signal −14.62, histogram −1.46. Three readings matter:
- The MACD line **crossed below zero on 2026-10-15** (−0.37) and has never recovered — the zero-line crossing preceded the 10/30 structural break by ~10 sessions.
- The MACD line has **essentially stopped declining**: −15.89 (11/20) → −15.85 (11/23) → −16.15 (11/24) → **−16.09 (11/25)**. The slope is flat.
- The histogram has **contracted three sessions running**: −2.62 (11/20) → −2.06 (11/23) → −1.89 (11/24) → **−1.46 (11/25)**.

So momentum is decelerating, but the histogram is still **negative** and there is **no bullish crossover** (MACD remains below signal). This is a "bears losing steam" configuration, not a "bulls in control" configuration.

**5.4 Momentum quality of the last bar.** The 2026-11-25 bar closed at $103.72 versus a low of $94.88 — a **+9.31% close-from-low recovery** — with a total range of $9.43 = **1.05 × ATR(8.95)**. That is a genuine volatility-expansion reversal bar, and it followed a decisive **failed breakdown**: price gapped below the 11/20 low ($101.71) and 11/24 low ($101.91), traded down to $94.88, and closed *back above* the broken zone. The measured-move objective of that failure (the $7.03 breakdown depth projected back up from $101.71–$101.91) targets **$108.74–$108.94**, which sits just under the 2026-11-23 high of $111.40 and below the 10 EMA.

## 6. Volatility

**ATR = 8.95, or 8.63% of the $103.72 close.** For a $100 stock this is enormous — a single average daily true range consumes nearly a ninth of the price. ATR has been *compressing* from its local peak of 11.14 (2026-10-16) to 8.95, a **−19.7%** decline, and has held in a tight 8.91–9.07 band across the last four sessions (9.07 on 11/23, 8.91 on 11/24, 8.95 on 11/25). **Volatility compression after a waterfall decline is itself a warning**: it typically resolves into expansion, and the 11/25 bar already delivered a 1.05-ATR range.

**Bollinger structure (verified snapshot, supplementary):** upper $161.94, middle (20 SMA) $127.22, lower $92.49. Band width is **$69.45 = 54.6% of the middle line** — an extreme expansion regime, not a compression regime (the bands are wide because the 20-day dispersion is enormous). Two specific facts:
- The 2026-11-25 low of **$94.88 came within $2.39 (2.6%) of the lower band at $92.49**. A near-tag of the lower band on an expanding band is not a reversal trigger, but it defines the natural downside reference and the level at which the "band touch" argument would have to resolve.
- The 20 SMA at **$127.22 is a more meaningful tactical reference than the 50 SMA** — it is 2.63 ATR above and is the average price of the last 20 sessions, so it approximates where the recent consolidation actually sits.

## 7. Volume

**VWMA = 117.76** (from $186.99 on 2026-10-12). Price at $103.72 is **11.92% below** the 20-day volume-weighted average. This gap is the market's own verdict: the average dollar spent on COIN over the last 20 sessions is materially above spot, meaning **distribution occurred well above the current price** — every rally into the $110–$120 zone is into trapped supply. This is why I rank VWMA as more informative here than a plain 20 SMA would be.

**Volume on the 2026-11-25 reversal: 9,823,149 shares.**
- 20-session average (10/29 → 11/25): **9.71M** → today's bar is **+1.1% vs average**, i.e., *in line*.
- 18-session average excluding the two capitulation spikes (10/30 at 20.89M and 11/20 at 14.19M): **8.84M** → today is **+11.1%** above that.
- Conclusion: **the reversal bar carries only marginal volume confirmation.** Real capitulation reversals in COIN have historically carried 15–20M+ shares (10/30: 20.89M; 11/20: 14.19M). A 9.8M-share reversal is a *convincing price action* but a *thin-volume* one — a signal that needs follow-through in the next 1–3 sessions to be trusted, and one that a seller can reverse on modest supply.

## 9. Actionable Trade Frameworks

**Setup A — Counter-trend relief long (highest probability of a *bounce*, lowest probability of a *trend change*).**
- Rationale: RSI bullish divergence (price lower low $101.71→$94.88 vs RSI higher low 22.94→28.68), MACD histogram contraction (−2.62→−1.46), a failed breakdown that closed back above $101.71–$101.91, and ATR contraction toward 8.91–9.07.
- Entry trigger: hold above **$101.71** and a close above **$104.31** (the 11/25 high). Do not front-run the trigger.
- Stop: **$93.00** (below the $94.88 low; = 1.20 ATR from entry, 10.72 points / 10.3%).
- Targets: **T1 $108.74–$108.94** (measured move, +5.0%), **T2 $113.04** (10 EMA, +9.0%), **T3 $127.22** (20 SMA, +22.7%).
- R-multiples from a $103.72 entry with a $93.00 stop (risk $10.72): **T1 ≈ 0.47R, T2 ≈ 0.87R, T3 ≈ 2.19R**. Only T3 clears a 2:1 hurdle — meaning this is, mechanically, a *low-R* setup and should be sized small.
- **This is a scalp/mean-reversion trade, not a position trade.** The November pattern is unambiguous: bounces are faded within 1–2 sessions (11/04 close 151.50 → 11/05 close 136.82, −9.7% in one session; 11/23 close 108.78 → 11/24 close 102.35, −5.9%).

**Setup B — Trend-continuation short (higher probability of *direction*, worse entry location).**
- Trigger: a decisive close **below $94.88**, ideally on volume ≥ 12M shares. This opens price discovery with no historical support beneath.
- Stop: reclaim of **$104.31** (the breakdown bar's high) — i.e., trade only on confirmed failure of the breakdown, not on a marginal breach.
- Targets: **$92.49** (lower band) first, then extension to ~**$85–87** (1.5–2 ATR below the low, the $76.98 2-ATR level being the maximum logical extension).
- Caveat: with RSI at 28.68, MACD histogram contracting, and the MACD line flat, the *timing* of a new short is poor even if the *direction* is right. Wait for the breakdown, don't anticipate it.

**Setup C — Trend-reversal long (the "prove it" trade).**
- Requirements, all three: (1) close above the **10 EMA $113.04** and hold it for two sessions; (2) the **10 EMA flattens** (it currently falls ~2.3 pts/day — a reclaim into a still-plunging EMA is a false signal); (3) the **MACD histogram crosses above zero** (currently −1.46).
- The next resistance band above that is $115.02–$119.84 (11/16–11/17 closes) and then $127.22 (20 SMA). A close above $127.22 would be the first credible medium-term regime shift and would justify a swing-length position.
- Invalidation: close back below $94.88.

**Setup D — Do not trade (the highest-probability outcome).** Price wedged between $94.88 and $113.04 with ATR at 8.95 and no volume confirmation. Any position here is a coin flip paying a 8.6% daily true range.

## 10. Risk Management

- **ATR-based stops, not percentage stops.** At ATR 8.95, a "tight" 3% stop ($99.6) sits *inside* a single average day's range and will be swept by noise. Minimum sensible stop distance: **1.2 ATR (10.7 pts)** for a counter-trend scalp, **1.5–2 ATR (13.4–17.9 pts)** for a swing position.
- **Position sizing example.** Risking 1% of a $100,000 account ($1,000) with the $93.00 stop from a $103.72 entry (risk $10.72/share) → **93 shares**. With a 2-ATR stop ($17.90) → **55 shares**. Note that COIN's 8.6% daily range means a single position at 93 shares carries ~$1,000 of *daily* mark-to-market noise on a $9,650 notional.
- **Overnight gap risk is the dominant risk.** The 2026-10-30 bar gapped from a $162.32 prior close to a $148.23 open and closed $143.54 — a 10.6% single-day loss. Any stop within one ATR of the market is exposed to gap-through. Stops sized at 1.5–2 ATR exist partly to absorb such gaps.
- **Size the counter-trend long at roughly half the normal allocation** given the 25% of ATR that the measured-move objective (T1 $108.74) sits below the 10 EMA ($113.04) — i.e., you are expected to be right on direction and wrong on the market's willingness to hold the gain.

---

## 1. Recent COIN-specific developments

A successful short-window news pull covering November 23–25 produced several relevant headlines. Wider company-news queries repeatedly failed, so this is not a complete seven-day company-news record.

### Buybacks provide a possible technical cushion

Reports during the week included:

Traders should verify whether these are issuer repurchases or open-market purchases by the CEO before incorporating them into a valuation model.

Buybacks can absorb supply and cushion volatility, but they do not directly offset a broad crypto selloff. With BTC downside odds increasing, treating the buyback alone as a durable bottom signal would be risky.

### Analyst sentiment improved

Wedbush initiated coverage of COIN and Robinhood at Outperform, according to [Investing.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wedbush-starts-robinhood-coinbase-outperform-163557118.html).

[TheStreet reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/coinbase-wins-dismissal-four-investor-182035156.html) that Coinbase won dismissal of a four-year investor lawsuit.

That is directionally favorable, but the available headline did not specify whether the dismissal is appealable, whether costs are payable, or whether related claims remain. It should not be treated as a complete elimination of litigation risk.

Armstrong’s comments about retail investors being excluded from private-market IPOs reinforce Coinbase’s tokenization narrative. Prediction markets, however, show investors pushing the expected timeline further out:

## 2. The dominant macro regime: restrictive rates without a recession

The most important finding is the combination of high hike odds and very low recession odds.

### December Fed meeting

Polymarket snapshots showed:

- **25-basis-point hike:** 94%, on approximately $13.5 million volume.
- **No change:** 4%, on approximately $16.6 million volume.
- **50-basis-point-or-larger hike:** 2%.
- A rate cut after the meeting: approximately 0%.

Additional contracts indicated:

- **No Fed cuts in 2026:** 98%, on approximately $9.9 million volume.
- **Two Fed hikes in 2026:** 92%.
- **Upper bound of the target federal funds rate at 4.25% at year-end:** 91%.

For January 2027, the market still gives a **54% probability of another 25-basis-point hike**, compared with 44% for no change and only about 3% for cuts. That suggests the market expects the restrictive policy path to extend beyond December, even though the confidence is lower than for December.

These are high-volume, relatively reliable crowd-implied probabilities, but they are still market prices rather than certainties.

### Recession risk remains low

The probability of a US recession by the end of 2026 is only **3%**, on approximately $2.5 million volume. The UK and Japan recession contracts are similarly low.

This is not automatically bullish for crypto. “No recession plus further Fed hikes” can describe a strong economy with financial conditions tightening because policymakers believe inflation remains persistent. [BeInCrypto’s discussion](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/why-america-goldilocks-economy-bad-175832972.html) explicitly framed the “Goldilocks” environment as problematic for Bitcoin and gold.

Low-volume November CPI contracts placed the largest single probability on a **0.1% monthly decline**, with 0.0% and a 0.2% decline also receiving meaningful odds. 1. **Transaction revenue** — retail and institutional trading spreads on BTC, ETH, SOL and stablecoins. Near-100% gross margin, but almost purely volume/price-driven and therefore the most cyclical line. This is what collapsed in 2026.
2. **Subscription & services revenue** — USDC balances (interest earned on customer stablecoin reserves and on COIN's own USDC holdings), custodial account fees, Coinbase One subscriptions, staking, and institutional data/prime services. This line is *rate-sensitive* (it shrinks as the Fed cuts) and is the historical source of the company's earnings floor.
3. **Interest income and other** — lending/margin, plus fair-value movements on the investment portfolio (crypto held for investment, equity stakes), which is a major driver of reported net income volatility.

**Key structural characteristics for traders:**
- **Asset-light:** tagged capital expenditure is effectively zero ($1–8M/yr through 2022; blank/nil thereafter). All investing cash flow is *financial* — crypto and USDC purchases — not capex.
